title: Power Automate: direct triggers for desktop flows
summary: Hold: the briefing overlooks published desktop-flow metering and casts existing module-level data policies as unconfirmed. It also omits a heading from the documented admin path and incorrectly says Learn describes only cloud-flow triggering. The roadmap status and target dates are accurate.

claims.claim: Data policies can govern desktop flow modules.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The desktop flow connector can be governed like other connectors.
claims.quote: The desktop flow connector can be governed in your policies like any other connector in all environments.

claims.claim: Adding desktop flow modules to a policy causes existing desktop flows to be evaluated against them.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them

claims.claim: Noncompliant desktop flows are suspended after policy evaluation.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: The documented path is Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. In the Data protection and privacy screen, select the Data policy section.
claims.fix: Change controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy', retaining the existing surface and docs URL. Settings is the documented group heading between Security and Data and privacy.

claims.claim: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell provides New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy to create a data policy.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies require Environment Admin permissions outside the Dataverse exception.

claims.claim: Environments with a Dataverse database require System Administrator instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.
